summary.text: Phil Ehr is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 28th Congressional District. He is a retired U.S. Navy officer who has run for Congress in prior cycles.

paragraphs.text: Born in Colorado and lived for many years in Pensacola before moving to West Kendall in Miami-Dade County, according to the Florida Keys Citizen.

Attended King's College London, earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of the State of New York and a master's degree in international relations from Troy State University.

Served in the U.S. Navy from 1982 to 2008 and retired as a commander; the Florida Keys Citizen reports his early assignments included the Mariel boatlift and work at Naval Air Station Key West with the Joint Interagency Task Force South.
Ran for Florida's 1st Congressional District in 2018 as a Democrat and lost the August primary to Jennifer Zimmerman, 60.5% to 39.5%.
Won the Democratic nomination in Florida's 1st District in 2020 after the primary was canceled, and lost the general election to Rep. Matt Gaetz, 64.6% to 34.0%.
Entered the 2024 U.S. Senate Democratic primary in Florida in July 2023, then withdrew in October 2023 to challenge Rep. Carlos Gimenez in the 28th District.
Lost the 2024 general election to Gimenez, 64.6% to 35.4%, and is again the Democratic nominee in 2026 after the August 18 primary was canceled.
